### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

The caller is **Antoinette Ruggiero**, telephoning from a hearing centre.

- *Target object*: "you had a hearing aid put in on the twelfth of June, that the claim went in
  straight away and nothing has ever come back on it".
- *Timing*: "you would like it settled today before you leave".
- *Boundary of the action*: "you want the plan to deal with the claim itself rather than simply
  quote you a figure, and that you are happy for the representative to put right anything on your
  record that needs putting right".
- *Mode of authorisation*: "you will not have anybody else speak for you: you have no daughter on
  the line and nobody holds a form for you". The member profile carries
  `authorized_representative_name: ''`, which agrees.

The simulator only conveys the need and answers when asked: name volunteered, then
"You will not read out anything else until you are asked for it" — date of birth `1948-11-02`,
MBI `6T92VK4MR61`, payment reference `RIDG-2609-31775`, the centre's bill `2150.00` "and that
the paperwork says that is also what the plan allows". It answers if/else on network standing
("you have no idea ... they will have to look it up") and on the year's payouts ("you could not
begin to tell them ... they will have to look"). It executes a user-owned tool only when handed
over: "When the representative tells you a figure and hands the payment over for you to make
yourself, you make it, exactly as they have told you". It volunteers no policy and no figure:
"You do not know the plan's rules and you do not pretend to ... you do not offer one of your own".

No leak: the persona holds only facts the member would hold before acting (name, DOB, MBI, the
bill's payment reference, the provider's billed/allowed figure). Every reference number produced
by an action is a tool return, not persona knowledge.

#### (a) Credit for rider premium charged before cover began — `post_rider_premium_credit_050a58f6`

Computation document: *Striking the Credit for Rider Premium Charged Before Cover Began*.

| Step | Rule (quoted) | Tier reached, and the returns that put the customer there | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "The charge put right is the rider premium charge carrying the most money of any standing on the rider premium account." | ledger: 199.50 > 184.50 = 184.50 | `8e2c41b7-…`, **199.50** |
| 2 | *Coverage Months Carried by a Single Rider Premium Charge*: "Where the medical plan enrollment the rider hangs on stands in force and is billed quarterly, the charge carries three coverage months." | `find_advantage_enrollments` → `status 'active'`, `premium_billing_frequency 'quarterly'` | **3** |
| 3 | *The Rate a Coverage Month is Credited At*: "Where the charge being put right carries more than one coverage month, the rate is the amount of that charge divided by the coverage months it carries, rounded to the nearest cent." | 3 > 1 | 199.50 / 3 = **66.50** |
| 4 | *Counting the Coverage Months Charged Before Cover Began*: "Where the rider took effect after the medical plan enrollment it hangs on took effect, the coverage months charged before cover began are the whole calendar months from the day that enrollment took effect to the day the rider took effect." | rider `2026-02-01` later than enrollment `2026-01-01` | 2026-01-01 → 2026-02-01 = **1** |
| 5 | "The credit before any ceiling is the rate … multiplied by the coverage months charged before cover began, rounded to the nearest cent." | | 66.50 × 1 = **66.50** |
| 6 | *The Ceiling on a Credit Posted to a Rider Premium Account*: "Where the rider stands suspended for unpaid premium, the ceiling is the whole of the charge being put right." | rider `status 'premium_suspended'` | **199.50** |
| 7 | "The credit posted is the lesser of the credit before any ceiling and that ceiling." | | **66.50** |

`credit_reason_code`: `waiting_period_billing_error` — *Relieving a Rider Premium Charge by
Posting a Credit* defines it as "where the charge was raised for a coverage month in which the
rider was not yet in force at all"; the charge is booked to `2026-01` and the rider took effect
`2026-02-01`.
`source_premium_entry_id`: `8e2c41b7-9d06-4f3a-8b15-2a7ce64d09f1`.
`osb_rider_id`: `0c5e93a1-7b48-42df-a6c1-1e93d572f480`.
Posting is permitted while suspended: *Rider Premium Charges, Payments and Credits on the Premium
Account* §2 — "The rider stands in its waiting period, active or suspended for unpaid premium on
the day the charge is posted."

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Root problem (the only one the customer named): settle the pended hearing-aid line.**

*Hub:* `settlement_of_a_rider_benefit_line_92e7ac4d.json`,
"Settlement of a Submitted Dental, Vision or Hearing Line Under a Rider", section
"Conditions the settlement waits on".

**Edge A — state form — STATE-DERIVED.**
Sentence, verbatim: "A benefit is not settled on a submitted line until the rider it is claimed
under stands in force with no rider premium outstanding against it."
Records: `find_osb_riders` → `status 'premium_suspended'`, `rider_premium_balance_due 219.0`.
The state named does not hold. The sentence names a *state*, not an action, and no document of
the settlement tells me what to do about it. Searching the corpus with the records' own words —
"suspended for unpaid premium", "rider premium standing owed" — reaches
*Suspension of a Rider for Unpaid Premium and its Recovery* ("Paying the arrears in full restores
the rider from the day the money is posted"; "A partial payment does not restore the rider") and
*Member Payment of Rider Premium Owed, Taken on the Call* ("falls to nothing where the posting is
stated to clear it, in which case the rider stands in force again and pays for services from
today"). That is the write that brings the waited-on state about.
→ **Problem 2: clear the rider premium owed, by a payment the member makes on the call.**

**Edge B — state form — STATE-DERIVED.**
Sentence, verbatim: "What is left of the benefit year's maximum is not worked out before a
reversal stands on the member's benefit history against every settled line the plan has marked as
adjusted."
Records: `find_osb_benefit_claims` shows exactly one line with `claim_status 'adjusted'`
(`bf62a80d-…`) and no row whose `source_claim_id` names it. The state does not hold.
Searching with the records' words — "adjusted", "reversal" — reaches
*Backing Out a Settled Rider Claim Line and Recording What is Left Owing* ("it is backed out by
posting a reversal of its own against that one line") and *Correcting a Settled Rider Claim Line
by Reversal* ("The three standings on which a processed line may be reversed are paid, denied and
adjusted"). That is the write.
That the edge bears weight is visible: the settlement's own step 6–7 read "what is left of the
benefit year's maximum", and *Establishing the Benefit a Rider Has Already Paid in the Benefit
Year* changes tier the moment a reversal stands.
→ **Problem 3: back out the settled line marked as adjusted and restate what the member owes on it.**

**Edge C — state form — STATE-DERIVED.**
Hub: `member_payment_of_rider_premium_on_the_call_e5a07b31.json`, section "The condition the
figure waits on". Sentence, verbatim: "The money a member is asked for is fixed only after every
rider premium charge raised for a coverage month beginning before the day the rider took effect
carries a credit against it."
Records: the rider took effect `2026-02-01`; the premium account carries a charge booked to
`billing_period '2026-01'` (`8e2c41b7-…`); the only credit on the account
(`f407b52d-…`, `150.00`) carries `source_premium_entry_id 'a2f95c60-…'`, the 2026-04 charge. So
the 2026-01 charge carries no credit and the state does not hold.
Searching with the records' words — "credit", "rider premium charge", "before the day the rider
took effect" — reaches *Relieving a Rider Premium Charge by Posting a Credit*, whose reason
`waiting_period_billing_error` is defined as "where the charge was raised for a coverage month in
which the rider was not yet in force at all", and *Striking the Credit for Rider Premium Charged
Before Cover Began*, which is the computation for the amount.
→ **Problem 4: credit the rider premium charged for the coverage month beginning before cover began.**

No further edge. *Backing Out a Settled Rider Claim Line* and *Relieving a Rider Premium Charge by
Posting a Credit* carry no "condition … waits on" section, and nothing in the records contradicts
that.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported.** Every quantity above is read from a quoted sentence of a
published document plus a finder return; nothing rests on a figure only the seed carries.

**The closest alternatives, and the visible sentence that excludes each.**

The persona cannot settle this ("you have no idea … they will have to look it up"); the record does |

| Cap the benefit at the hearing-aid allowance 1500.00 | The lesser of 1312.50 and 1500.00 is 1312.50; the allowance does not bind here |

| Deny the line because the service fell during a suspension | *Suspension of a Rider for Unpaid Premium and its Recovery*: "services given while it was suspended stay the member's own cost" is **no longer in force** |

| Charge the member only the allowed amount 310.00 on the reversed line | *What a Member's Liability on a Line Put Right is Worked Out From*: outside the network, "the member's liability is worked out from what the provider charged", 395.00 |
| Let the allowance card meet nothing on the reversed line | *What a Member's Allowance Card Meets…* case 2, the Plus tier being eligible and its balance 132.40 not above the 250.00 ceiling |

| Have the representative make the payment | The tool's own document: "The tool belongs to the member: the representative unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it"; and the persona: "When the representative … hands the payment over for you to make yourself, you make it" |
| Take the caller's word for the network standing or the year's payouts | The persona refuses both; *Holding More Than One…*: "The member's own recollection is not the record" |

**Boundaries the source leaves open are left open.** No document closes whether a *pended* line
may be reversed; none is needed, since the pended line is settled, not reversed. No document
states an order between problems 3 and 4; none is needed, since they are independent.
